Talbot Heath Head of Sport Selected for Globally Recognised PE Scholar Associate Programme
Talbot Heath School is celebrating National Fitness Day by recognising a significant professional achievement for Head of PE and Sport Dept, Lou Lindon, who has been selected as a PE Scholar Associate 2026/27, joining a prestigious international network of educators committed to advancing excellence in physical education, physical activity and school sport.
Following a rigorous and highly competitive application process, Lou was chosen as one of a select group of PE professionals from across the UK and around the world. Her appointment recognises her expertise, leadership and commitment to ensuring high-quality physical education, physical activity and sporting experiences for all students.
Lou Lindon’s selection reflects Talbot Heath’s longstanding commitment to providing outstanding opportunities in sport and physical education. From recreational participation to elite-level performance pathways, the school’s extensive programme encourages every pupil to develop confidence, resilience and a lifelong love of being active.
This commitment extends beyond the sports field. Students have the opportunity to study GCSE and A Level Physical Education, gaining a deeper understanding of the science, psychology and sociology of sport, while the nationally recognised Level 3 Sports Leaders Award enables students to develop valuable leadership, coaching and event management skills through practical experience and community engagement.
As a PE Scholar Associate, Lou will collaborate with leading practitioners from across the profession, contributing ideas, resources and research-informed practice designed to enhance physical education provision and outcomes for young people.
Commenting on her appointment, Lou said:
“I am delighted to have been selected as a PE Scholar Associate and to be working alongside such an inspiring group of professionals. Physical education has the power to positively impact every young person’s life, and I am passionate about ensuring all students have access to high-quality experiences that help them thrive.”
Talbot Heath Head, Ross Cameron, added:
“This is a fantastic achievement for Lou and a reflection of the passion, expertise and innovation she brings to our PE and sport provision. We are delighted to see her recognised through this globally respected programme and look forward to the opportunities it will create for our pupils, staff and wider sporting community.”
Lou’s appointment provides further recognition of the strength of Talbot Heath’s sporting provision and its commitment to inspiring the next generation to lead active, healthy and fulfilling lives.

HEAD’S BLOG: Beyond Grades, Redefining Success for the Next Generation
As schools across the country celebrate another set of examination results, it is a moment to acknowledge the hard work, dedication and ambition of young people. Outstanding academic outcomes deserve to be celebrated. They represent years of effort, perseverance and commitment, and they open doors to exciting opportunities.
At Talbot Heath, we have recently celebrated exceptional A Level results, 54% A* to A, 81% A* to B, with students securing places at leading universities and taking their next steps with confidence. We are immensely proud of what they have achieved.
Yet while academic excellence matters deeply, results alone do not tell the whole story.
Ask a group of parents what they ultimately want for their children and the answers are remarkably consistent. We want them to be happy, fulfilled and capable of leading meaningful lives. We want them to thrive not only in their careers, but also in their relationships, their communities and their sense of purpose.
Academic success plays an important part in that journey. Education opens doors and creates opportunities. However, the qualities that enable young people to flourish in the long term often extend far beyond examination grades.
Resilience, curiosity, adaptability, kindness and integrity are increasingly recognised as essential attributes in a complex and fast-changing world. They influence how we respond to setbacks, embrace new opportunities and contribute to the lives of others. They shape not just what we achieve, but who we become.
The reality is that many of today’s young people will pursue careers that do not yet exist. They will navigate technological change, global uncertainty and evolving workplaces. Success will depend not only on knowledge and qualifications, but also on creativity, collaboration and the confidence to keep learning throughout life.
I often meet former pupils whose paths have taken unexpected turns. Some have become leaders in their professions. Others have followed passions that emerged long after they left school. What unites them is not a perfect academic record, but a sense of purpose, adaptability and the courage to seize opportunities.
The strongest schools understand that academic excellence and character development are not competing priorities. In fact, they reinforce one another. Young people who are confident, engaged and intellectually curious are often those who achieve the highest standards academically.
So while we rightly celebrate examination success, we should remember what those results represent. Behind every grade is a young person who has grown in confidence, developed resilience and discovered something about their own potential.
If education can equip young people with both outstanding qualifications and the character to use them wisely, then we will have achieved something truly meaningful. Not simply success in examinations, but success in life.
Ross Cameron, Talbot Heath Head

Talbot Heath is currently ranked as Dorset’s highest-performing girls’ school for A Level A* to A grades
Talbot Heath School is celebrating an exceptional set of A Level results, with students achieving some of the strongest outcomes in the school’s recent history.
An impressive 54% of all grades were awarded at A* or A, almost double the current national average of 28.3%. In addition, 81% of grades were achieved at A* to B, alongside a remarkable 100% pass rate, highlighting the academic excellence, resilience and determination of Talbot Heath students.
Further cementing its reputation for academic excellence, Talbot Heath is currently ranked as Dorset’s highest-performing girls’ school for A Level A* to A grades, based on the latest published 2026 results.
This year’s cohort has a particularly inspiring story to tell. Having begun their secondary education in September 2019, they had been in school for only a matter of months before the national lockdown of March 2020 transformed education across the country. Despite the unprecedented disruption to their formative years, they adapted with remarkable maturity, embraced new ways of learning and approached every challenge with determination and resilience.
Throughout that period, Talbot Heath ensured that students continued to receive a first-class education, seamlessly transitioning to high-quality online learning and maintaining the close support and academic guidance for which the school is renowned. The results achieved today are a powerful testament to the students’ perseverance and the strength of the Talbot Heath community.
Several students have secured a full set of A* grades, while leavers are progressing to an impressive range of prestigious destinations and degree programmes. These include Biomedical Sciences at Imperial College London, one of the world’s leading institutions for science and medicine; Veterinary Science at the University of Liverpool; Acting at the highly competitive Central School of Speech and Drama; Music at Durham University; and History at the University of Exeter. Many students have also secured places at leading Russell Group universities.
Head, Ross Cameron, said:
“I am absolutely thrilled by these outstanding results and delighted for our students. They are thoroughly deserved and reflect years of hard work, ambition and determination. This cohort of pupils has faced significant challenges during their school journey, and have shown extraordinary resilience and character in meeting these challenges so successfully.
“We are immensely proud of everything that they have achieved. Their success is also a reflection of the exceptional dedication of our staff and the strong partnership between our school and pour families. At Talbot Heath, our small class sizes and personalised approach mean that every student is known, valued and supported as an individual. Today’s results demonstrate the impact of that bespoke educational experience, and we look forward to seeing our students thrive as they embark on the next stages of their journeys in life.”
These results once again underline Talbot Heath’s reputation for outstanding teaching, exceptional pastoral care and a commitment to helping every student fulfil their potential. As this talented cohort moves on to exciting futures, they leave Talbot Heath with achievements of which they, their families and the entire school community are immensely proud.

Senior school 11-16 Careers Guidance
Careers Guidance
At Talbot Heath, we want all of our students to make well informed and realistic choices about their future lives and careers. Careers information, education and guidance (CIEG) enables young people to become effective planners and managers of their own careers. The world is changing at a fast pace, so we support students to make good decisions for themselves and to manage the transitions from further education to the world of work. We focus on the employability skills that our students need for a successful career in the 21st Century; resilience, communication, team work, problem solving and curiosity are valued greatly by employers.
We help our students to find out what they want to do, and who they want to be when they complete their formal education. We encourage them to think about what they love, what they are good at, and to find a career that aligns with their passions and skills.
We allow our students to develop and practise the self-help skills they need to progress their own career plans and development, including making discerning use of careers information, advice and guidance, available at school and elsewhere. The Careers team keep students up to date with current trends in assemblies and careers sessions; they also have links to online webinars and careers information.
The Head of Careers and form tutors deliver the careers programme and ensure that it is relevant to each of their tutees, advising them individually as appropriate.
We consider it very important that students make GCSE and A-level choices relevant to their own situation. Therefore each pupil has a personal interview with the Head of Careers and access to a fully qualified advisor if needed.
Students also have the chance to be involved in many other exciting opportunities such as National Apprenticeship Week, National Careers Week and My Money Week. Green Careers Week in the autumn term is a UK wide celebration; our students will continue the exploration of Green Jobs, Green Skills and the Green Economy with our own Talbot Heath sustainability week in the summer term.
Please contact our Head of Careers, Mrs Manley, if you need any more information.
smanley@talbotheath.org
During this year the importance of setting targets and how they can help to achieve goals will be explained. Pupils will have the opportunity to explore their own skills and qualities and how these can help in identifying their strengths and possible career interests. They will also have the chance to develop their teamwork skills during charity week planning.
During this year pupils will review target setting and study skills. They will explore job families, budgeting and understanding about work and employability. They will spend time developing their career research skills, and learn how to make decisions.
During this year the girls will make some important choices about their GCSE option subjects. Before choosing these subjects they will be given the opportunity to talk to subject staff, as well as L5 (year 10) girls who are already studying that subject. They will also have an interview with the Head of Careers if required, to discuss possible career aspirations and how these might influence their subject choice. They will also be given the opportunity to attend a Careers Convention to discuss career possibilities with employers, universities etc. At the end of the year they are introduced to Unifrog, a destinations platform.
During this year the girls will use web-based skills and interests questionnaires, to suggest possible careers linked to their skills and interests. They will consider the rights and responsibilities of employers and employees and be made aware of the laws to protect school age students whilst working. They will also participate in the Sixth Form Taster Day when they are given the opportunity to find out more about A level subjects, as well as life in the Sixth Form. During the day the Head of Careers, Head of Sixth Form, Sixth Form Tutors, as well as Subject Staff, are all available to answer any questions about careers, A level courses, and life in the Sixth form, as are current members of the Sixth form.
During this year the girls will make some important decisions which may affect their future career. We will support and advise them so that they are able to make sensible and informed choices, about their A level subjects or other courses. The girls will have an interview with the Head of Careers, as well as the opportunity to attend the Sixth Form Open Evening and talk to subject staff about A level courses, including the Extended Project Qualification. They will be given advice on how to prepare for an interview and they will also prepare a CV and Personal Statement.
Sixth form (Years 12 and 13)
It is essential that the girls carefully research all options available to them after they leave school at the end of Upper 6. The sixth form tutors offer support to their tutees and encourage them to make choices most suitable to their ability and interests. This is done in conjunction with subject staff. The Head of Careers is also available for one-to-one discussions.
The majority of our Sixth Formers go onto university and the girls are encouraged to thoroughly research all options before making their application; extensively using Unifrog. There are also books and university prospectuses available in the Careers section of the school library to help with this.
Any girl who is considering not going to University will be advised by both her tutor and the Head of Careers, to ensure that she makes an informed decision about her future career, including Apprenticeship and Gap Year options . They will also be given the opportunity to attend a Careers Convention to discuss career aspirations with employers, universities etc.
Many girls will undertake Work Experience, Voluntary Work or attend courses that are relevant to her future Career. This may include targeted talks e.g. Oxford and Cambridge application. Mock interviews are arranged, with feedback, for those girls who apply to Oxford or Cambridge University, and for those applying to courses such as Medicine or Veterinary Science.

pageCache.text:
Psychology Students Explore History, Culture and Human Behaviour in Vienna
Our A Level Psychology students recently enjoyed an enriching and memorable trip to Vienna, Austria, bringing many aspects of their studies to life through a fascinating programme of educational visits and cultural experiences.
One of the highlights of the trip was a visit to the Narrenturm (Fool’s Tower) Anatomical Museum, housed within what was originally Europe’s oldest purpose-built institution for psychiatric patients. Students explored a range of real anatomical specimens and medical conditions, making valuable connections to their Biopsychology studies and deepening their understanding of the relationship between the brain, behaviour and physical health.
The group also visited the Mauthausen Memorial concentration camp, an experience that provided a powerful opportunity for reflection. Students considered the psychological and historical factors that contributed to the Holocaust, linking their observations to topics including social influence, destructive obedience and Adorno’s Authoritarian Personality Theory.
Another key visit took students to the former home and practice of Sigmund Freud, where they explored the origins of psychoanalysis and gained a deeper appreciation of Freud’s influence on the development of the psychodynamic approach to understanding human behaviour.
Alongside the academic programme, students immersed themselves in Vienna’s rich culture and history. They explored many of the city’s famous landmarks, enjoyed thrilling rides at the iconic Prater amusement park and sampled traditional Viennese cuisine. They also became remarkably adept at navigating Vienna’s excellent transport system, confidently travelling across the city by tram, underground, train and even Uber.
The trip provided an outstanding combination of psychology, history and cultural exploration, enabling students to see classroom concepts in a real-world context while creating unforgettable memories. Throughout the visit, our students represented the school exceptionally well, demonstrating curiosity, maturity and enthusiasm at every stage of the journey.
We are delighted to have been able to offer such a rewarding experience, combining academic enrichment with cultural discovery and helping to inspire the next generation of psychologists.
We must thank Team Snell for giving our students this fantastic experience.

Talbot Heath Welcomes National Focus on Work Experience and Invites Local Businesses to Inspire the Next Generation
Talbot Heath School has welcomed last week’s renewed focus on work experience for young people, following Prime Minister Mayor Andy Burnham’s announcement highlighting the importance of ensuring every young person has access to meaningful workplace opportunities.
At Talbot Heath, this commitment is already firmly embedded within the Sixth Form experience. Every student undertakes a compulsory work experience programme, spending one afternoon each week with a local employer from October through to Easter. The extended format allows students to become valued members of a team, gain a genuine understanding of a profession and develop the confidence, skills and experience that employers and universities increasingly value.
The school is now looking to strengthen its network of employer partners and is inviting more organisations in the Bournemouth, Poole and Christchurch area to get involved.
Ross Cameron, Head of Talbot Heath School, said:
“Work experience should be more than a one-week snapshot. By spending a regular afternoon each week with an employer over several months, our students have the opportunity to build relationships, contribute meaningfully and gain a much deeper understanding of the workplace.”
“Our aim is to ensure every Sixth Form student leaves Talbot Heath not only with excellent academic qualifications but also with the confidence, professional skills and real-world experience to thrive in higher education and beyond. We are incredibly grateful to the businesses that already support us and would love to hear from more organisations that are passionate about investing in the next generation.”
Talbot Heath is keen to partner with businesses and organisations from a wide range of sectors. Placements in any profession are welcomed, helping to reflect the diverse ambitions of the school’s students.
Hosting a student for one afternoon each week offers businesses the opportunity to share their expertise, support young people’s career aspirations and strengthen connections with the local community. Many employers find that students quickly become valued members of the team while bringing fresh ideas, enthusiasm and curiosity to the workplace.
The programme forms part of Talbot Heath’s wider commitment to careers education, ensuring students can make informed decisions about their futures through meaningful encounters with employers and professionals.
Businesses based in the Bournemouth, Poole and Christchurch area that would be interested in hosting a Sixth Form student between October and Easter are encouraged to contact Mrs Hawes via the office to find out more about becoming a work experience partner. office@talbotheath.org

Senior School Curriculum
What is our CURRICULUM?
The curriculum serves as the backbone of education, shaping the learning experiences and opportunities for every student. It provides a structured framework through which knowledge, skills, and values are imparted, ensuring a comprehensive and well-rounded education. A well-designed curriculum not only facilitates academic excellence but also promotes critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving abilities essential for success in the modern world.
Moreover, the curriculum reflects the values and priorities of the school, fostering a sense of community, identity, and shared purpose among students and educators. By continually reviewing and enhancing our curriculum, we can adapt to the evolving needs of society, incorporate innovative teaching practices, and provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to thrive in an ever-changing global landscape. Therefore, investing in the development and refinement of our curriculum is paramount to fulfilling our mission of nurturing well-rounded individuals prepared for the challenges and opportunities of the future.
How do we do this?
At Talbot Heath we are future facing and prepare our young women for the challenges of the future. To that end our new vision has a dual focus on Sustainability for Learning and Artificial Intelligence.
Learning for Sustainability
Sustainability is at the forefront of our commitment. We recognise the importance of preserving our environment for future generations and aim to integrate sustainable practices into all aspects of our operations. From reducing our carbon footprint and conserving natural resources to promoting eco-friendly initiatives and educating our students about environmental stewardship, sustainability will be woven into the fabric of our school culture. By prioritising sustainability, we strive to instill a sense of responsibility and environmental consciousness in our students, empowering them to become agents of positive change in their communities and beyond.
Explore qualification options for subsequent years
Artificial Intelligence
In today’s rapidly evolving technological landscape, integrating education about artificial intelligence (AI) is paramount for preparing students to navigate and thrive in the future. As AI continues to permeate various aspects of society, from healthcare to finance, understanding its principles and applications becomes increasingly essential. Teaching about AI not only equips students with technical skills relevant to emerging industries but also cultivates critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and ethical considerations necessary for responsible AI development and implementation.
By incorporating AI education into our curriculum, we empower students to harness the transformative potential of AI while fostering a deeper understanding of its societal impacts, thus preparing them to become informed and proactive contributors to an AI-driven world.
Senior Trips
Talbot Heath School offers a diverse range of Senior School trips that enrich students’ learning experiences. These journeys encompass both educational and recreational destinations. There are cultural visits to Bath, a thought-provoking trip to Shepton Mallet Prison, geographical studies of the New Forest, Living Rainforest, Durdle Door and Lulworth Cove, historical insights at Hampton Court, Science trips to Monkey World, Leeson House and Marwell Zoo and regular engaging theatre outings for drama and music enthusiasts.
We also offer international trips to places like Rome, Spain and Greece and Austria and as far afield as New York, Japan, Borneo, Rwanda (to support the school’s charity Godfrey’s Village of Hope), and in 2025 Costa Rica. Not forgetting exhilarating ski adventures in France and Italy.
These diverse excursions contribute significantly to the students’ holistic education and global perspectives.

Nursery and Kindergarten (Age 2+)
At Talbot Heath, we create a truly home-from-home atmosphere, and our stimulating environment is thoughtfully designed to promote all seven areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum. Central to our philosophy is child-led learning which is enriched with inspiring topics that engage and enthuse young minds.
We offer multi-sensory learning opportunities ensuring every pupil thrives. Our dedicated specialist Early Years practitioners guide your daughter through this exciting journey; emphasising our core values of curious minds, adventurous spirits and generous hearts.
Curiosity is at the heart of our approach as we follow the interests of our pupils, fostering a love for exploration and discovery. Pupils are encouraged to share, listen and develop strong relationships with peers and adults; ultimately preparing them for a bright and compassionate future.
We promote a spirit of adventure and a ‘have a go attitude’ encouraging independence and resilience; creating a safe environment where our pupils are encouraged to assess, consider and take risks confidently. Our aim is to instil a lifelong love of learning!
From the age of 2, pupils benefit from high quality teaching and learning session which focus on communication and language, personal, social and emotional development and physical development We encourage our pupils to explore the world around them – whatever the weather – and nurture this through our weekly Forest School session within our beautiful woodland campus and outdoor Roundhouse classroom.
As they turn 3 years old, pupils also have access to weekly French, PE, Yoga, Drama and Music lessons, all taught by specialist teachers. In addition, they also have a fortnightly swimming lesson in our onsite, indoor pool.
Throughout your daughter’s Early Years journey, we are committed to providing a strong foundation and a smooth, confident transition into our Reception year. Our pupils benefit from regular opportunities to work alongside and interact with older pupils, attend school assemblies and events; helping to build confidence, social skills and a sense of belonging within our wider school community.
*We are currently up to capacity for two year olds, you are welcome to visit and apply with a view to your child starting after their 3rd birthday.
As well as accepting Early Years funding and childcare vouchers, Nursery fees are VAT exempt, offering parents financial peace of mind. Our Nursery is open from 8 am to 5.30 pm in term time. Early Years funding and childcare vouchers can be used between the hours of 8.30 am to 3.30 pm. If you would like to visit our wonderful Nursery you would be very welcome. Sport
PE and Sport at Talbot Heath is taught from Kindergarten through to 6th form, including GCSE and A-Level. As a department, we aim to address a vast range of skills, values and qualities.
Talbot Heath has fantastic sports facilities including: a heated swimming pool, fitness suite, sports hall, gymnasium, outdoor netball courts, tennis courts, full size astro turf and a generous field used for a variety of sporting events. Through the range of experiences that PE at Talbot Heath offers, pupils learn how to be effective in competitive, creative and challenging situations.
Talbot Heath Swimming Academy Building on the success of our renowned Tennis Academy, the Swimming Academy, an affiliated club with Swim England, is a leading destination for young female swimmers in the UK.
Talbot Heath Tennis Academy The Talbot Heath/West Hants High Performance Tennis Academy is designed to allow girls to combine tennis training and academic education into one integrated curriculum. Pupils are offered places if they show outstanding ability in their sport and pass the entrance examination. Talbot Heath is the number 3 Tennis School for Girls in the UK.
Our P.E. Curriculum Our PE department inspires, engages and motivates all pupils to enjoy leading healthy active lifestyles. We provide a broad and balanced curriculum which includes varied sporting opportunities. PE plays an important role in the personal and social development of pupils as well as ensuring they have a chance to play, compete and excel in a multitude of disciplines.
Extra Curricular Sports Clubs Extra-curricular PE clubs are run to enable pupils to pursue their interest in particular sporting activities or simply to keep active and have fun. There are a variety clubs of across the year including netball, football, fitness, badminton and pickleball, fencing, lacrosse, cross-country, tennis, rounders, cricket and athletics.
Clubs also provide specialised coaching and emphasis is placed on tactics and strategies as well as fitness and game play. Teams compete at local level and often reach County, Regional and National Finals and we are very proud of the sporting successes of pupils who compete Internationally in numerous sports. Some examples may include basketball, use of the fitness suite, swimming, wellbeing walks, rounders, tennis or dodgeball.
Sports Leaders Award – Year 12 Pupils have the opportunity to sign up for the Level 3 Sports Leaders Award in year 12. This nationally recognised qualification with 16 UCAS points. It is a great course which develops pupils’ ability to communicate, work as a group and problem solve.

Senior School 11-16
Senior School should be an exciting adventure for young people; it should be the springboard for their hopes and dreams; it should open their eyes to new subjects and possibilities and should develop their self-confidence and character.
In Senior School we welcome girls from our Junior School, as well as from a wide range of schools locally, nationally and internationally. Our pupils are broad in their interests and personalities but are united in their positive attitude to education. Pupils can be themselves within the school environment, which is especially important during adolescence.
Pupils and staff have great affection for their school and take great pride in it.
Ours is an education that prepares pupils for the exciting future that awaits them. They leave us as principled, confident, resilient and knowledgeable young women, ready to take their place in a global society.
“A gem of a school that is making waves in the education world thanks to its inspiring head and exciting approach to learning. Girls get a first-class education in a safe, caring and encouraging environment – and the school excels at supporting talented sport and music specialists too.”

At Talbot Heath, we understand that choosing an independent education is both a significant investment and a deeply personal decision for families. As we plan our academic and financial priorities each year, we remain committed to delivering exceptional value. We are proud to offer a continuous educational pathway from ages 2 to 18 and our fees reflect the stage of your child’s educational journey.
At the heart of our financial planning is a commitment to quality, value, and long-term sustainability. Each year, our budget is carefully reviewed to ensure that every element of expenditure is both essential and impactful—delivering meaningful educational outcomes while supporting the long-term sustainability of the school. We strive to keep increases to a minimum while continuing to invest in outstanding teaching, excellent facilities, and enriching experiences that help every pupil thrive.
We are here to support you at every step please don’t hesitate to get in touch with our Head of Admissions, Mrs Campbell-McLean, Email: admissions@talbotheath.org if you have any questions.
